classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied congruent trapeziums to construct a parallelogram and justify a general area formula by relating its base, height and doubled area.

content.prompt: Prove that the area of a trapezium is $\tfrac12h(a+b)$ by pasting together two identical trapeziums $ABCD$ and $A'B'C'D'$.

spec.description: Paired source trapeziums for the joining proof.
spec.mathematics: Preserve source labels, givens, side markers and all mathematically meaningful relationships. No additional right angle is supplied.

sizing.exceptionReason: A meaningful pair of labelled trapeziums must remain side by side for the joining proof, with complete vertex labels, matching side labels and height dimension.

answer.short: $A=\tfrac12h(a+b)$. Join the trapeziums to form a parallelogram of base $a+b$ and height $h$.
answer.worked: Join side $BC$ to side $B'C'$ so that $B$ meets $C'$ and $C$ meets $B'$. The two identical trapeziums form a parallelogram of base $a+b$ and perpendicular height $h$. Its area is $h(a+b)$, so each trapezium has area $\tfrac12h(a+b)$.
